subject: Confirming reserved GPU top-up and spillover behavior for renewal
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal discussion — reserved GPU top-up and spillover behavior

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Per our renewal cadence, you mentioned wanting to secure additional baseline capacity for Q4 to support the new personalization pipeline. To summarize my proposal:

- Add 8x V100-equivalent reserved GPUs to your Dedicated pool (committed 12 month term)
- Maintain your current preferred region (us-west-2) and pin model revisions used in production
- Throughput guarantee: 2.8 tokens/sec per lane (90th pct) with priority routing on committed capacity

We should also decide on how you'd like burst/overflow to behave when committed capacity is saturated. Two paths we typically see:

A) Hard cap: requests beyond reserved capacity return 429 / queue with an SLA-backed overflow denial. Lower unpredictable spend, but you need to handle client-side retry.

B) On-demand spillover: overflow routes to shared on-demand capacity at a per-token overage rate; keeps user-facing requests live but increases unit cost and may have wider latency variance.

Attached an updated pricing PDF and the burst matrix we discussed. Can you confirm (1) the preferred burst model (A or B), (2) whether you want the 8 GPUs reserved or prefer a 6 GPU top-up plus a 2 GPU burst buffer, and (3) procurement timeline so we can align PO/DocuSign?

If it's helpful I can loop in Jordan from our platform team to confirm routing policies and Marissa for CS-run canary windows.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
+1 415 555 0126

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pricing-v3.pdf, ssp-burst-matrix.xlsx

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme-retail.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — reserved GPU top-up and spillover behavior

Evelyn,

Thanks for the clear write-up. Couple of notes/questions from our side after reviewing the attachments and last week's PO forecast:

- We're leaning toward a 6 GPU reserved + 2 GPU burst buffer (option you called out). The reason is we expect steady baseline growth but want a small cushion without committing to full 8 GPUs up-front.
- For spillover, Procurement prefers the hard cap model for predictability in our cost forecasting. That said, our product team is worried about queueing impact on peak events (flash sales).
- Can you provide rough cost delta between (A) hard cap + pre-purchased burst credits (we'd buy in 100k-token blocks) vs (B) pure on-demand overage? Need that for the approval packet.
- Also: we have a policy constraint that any vendor overage above 20% month-over-month needs exec sign-off (so we need clear telemetry).

I'm attaching our August utilization snapshot for your reference. Our procurement timeline: we need signed terms in the week of Oct 5 to hit our internal vendor onboarding schedule.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Alex
Alex Turner
Head of ML Infrastructure, Acme Retail
acme-retail.com
Attachments: acme-current-utilization-aug2026.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme-retail.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-22T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — reserved GPU top-up and spillover behavior

Alex, Evelyn — thanks for the context. Quick cost/ops breakdown and two implementation patterns we can propose in the term addendum: 

1) Pricing sketch (illustrative):
  - 6x reserved GPUs (12-month commit): $56,400/mo (blended price inclusive of model-specific kernels)
  - 2x reserved burst buffer (soft-reserve with lower priority routing): $18,000/mo
  - Option A (Hard cap + pre-purchased burst credits): pre-burn credits priced at $0.0025/token for 100k-token blocks; credits apply only when requests exceed committed lanes; unused credits carry a 60-day rollover.
  - Option B (On-demand spillover): overage priced at $0.0040/token, billed monthly; no credit rollover.

2) Behavioral differences (operational):
  - Hard cap + credits: deterministic throttling when credits exhausted. Predictable spend with exposure limited to purchased credits; ideal for finance-sensitive customers.
  - On-demand: seamless user experience with higher spend variance; we include per-route latency buckets in Redwood Console to help set alerts.

3) Throughput & SLA commitments:
  - We will document a 90th percentile throughput guarantee on reserved lanes (2.8 tokens/sec per lane) with an uptime SLA for the dedicated pool. Spillover latency will be documented as best-effort for on-demand.

4) Next steps / mechanics:
  - If you choose hard cap + credits, we can add a schedule to the MSA that specifies block sizes and rollover terms.
  - If you choose on-demand, we recommend a 30-day canary window for the first month of the renewal so we can tune batching/cache and watch cost.

Reference files: attached "ssp-burst-matrix.xlsx" shows historic spill patterns and simulated cost for both models using your Aug utilization.

For procurement timelines: Oct 5 window looks achievable. I'll get a formal term sheet + price table ready by Sept 24. Jordan — can you confirm routing fallback details (region-level priorities + per-tenant cache limits) so I can include them in the term sheet?

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme-retail.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-23T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — reserved GPU top-up and spillover behavior

Looping in a CS perspective. A few practical recommendations if Acme picks hard cap + credits: 

- We'll set per-route SLIs and alerting in Redwood Console and provide a shared dashboard (read-only) for Acme's on-call.
- Propose a 14-day canary window post-activation for their personalization route to validate latency and failure modes — CS will run two synthetic workloads (normal & flash-sale) and share the results.
- For the 100k-token credit blocks: suggest we front-load one block at activation to avoid immediate throttles during the first peak events.

Also: can Legal confirm language around credit rollover (60 days) and whether unused credits are refundable on early termination? I'll defer to Contract on that point.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme-retail.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-24T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — reserved GPU top-up and spillover behavior

Alex / Procurement,

Thanks — this is all helpful. Summary / path forward we can commit to immediately if acceptable: 

1) Contractual commitment: 6x reserved GPUs + 2x soft-reserve burst buffer on a 12-month renewal term.
2) Burst policy: Hard cap by default + pre-purchased credits (we recommend an initial purchase of 300k-token credits to provide runway). Credits priced per Karthik's table; 60-day rollover. Legal to confirm non-refundability on early termination (we'll flag).
3) Ops: 14-day canary for personalization route; CS (Marissa) to provide dashboards and synthetic tests. Jordan to confirm routing fallback config and make sure cache warming is enabled before go-live.
4) Timeline: we will send a term addendum + pricing schedule by Sept 24. DocuSign envelope targeted the week of Sept 28 and execution by Oct 5 to meet your onboarding window.

Please reply with a single email that says "Approved — proceed to DocuSign" if this captures your intent, and I'll start the DocuSign/PO workflow.

Best regards,
Evelyn
